zBkNBP00wJE.summary: Jason Turner's CppCon 2016 talk builds a simple Commodore 64 game using C++17, showing how constexpr and const let a modern compiler produce tight 6502 code. He walks through assembly output to show abstractions being optimized away.
zBkNBP00wJE.why: A perennial favorite, recommended as proof that expressive modern C++ can compile to efficient code even on tiny retro hardware.

zDZFcDGpL4U.summary: An RSA Animate drawn from a Sir Ken Robinson talk arguing that current education systems are modeled on the industrial age. It discusses divergent thinking, standardization, and how schools disengage kids.
zDZFcDGpL4U.why: HN recommends it as an accessible, widely shared critique of schooling, and cites it in threads on ADHD, creativity and education reform.

z1ROpIKZe-c.summary: CGP Grey explains the City of London's unusual governance, including the Lord Mayor, guilds, and how it differs from the rest of London.
z1ROpIKZe-c.why: A favorite entry point to the weird history and privileges of the City of London.

zNVQfWC_evg.summary: David Tong, a Cambridge theoretical physicist, explains at the Royal Institution that the fundamental building blocks of nature are quantum fields rather than particles. He covers what we know about these fields and how they fit into the Standard Model.
zNVQfWC_evg.why: Called a favorite and a masterpiece by commenters as the clearest accessible explanation that there are only waves in fields, and what physics still doesn't know.

zb7Bs98KmnY.summary: Technology Connections examines why light bulbs have the lifespans they do, including the real history of the Phoebus cartel. He shows that bulb life trades off against brightness and efficiency rather than being simple planned obsolescence.
zb7Bs98KmnY.why: HN's go-to link for correcting the lightbulb conspiracy myth, giving an engineer's view of the lifespan versus efficiency tradeoff.

zjkBMFhNj_g.summary: Andrej Karpathy gives a one-hour general-audience introduction to large language models, covering what they are, how they are trained, comparisons to operating systems, and security challenges such as jailbreaks.
zjkBMFhNj_g.why: HN recommends it as the dense, approachable starting point for understanding LLMs and often cites it for specific claims about scaling and training.

zwAD6dRSVyI.summary: 3Blue1Brown visualizes high-dimensional spheres to explain a surprising puzzle about how a sphere fits in a box as dimensions grow. It builds geometric intuition for counterintuitive properties of high-dimensional space.
zwAD6dRSVyI.why: HN recommends it as the go-to intuitive visualization of high-dimensional geometry, relevant to machine learning, optimization and sphere packing.

z6yL0_sDnX0.summary: Episode 4 of James Burke's Connections series, tracing how commercialism, climate change and the Black Death shaped the move to the Renaissance. It follows threads through waterpower, the printing press, the Jacquard loom and the Hollerith punch card toward modern computing.
z6yL0_sDnX0.why: HN commenters strongly recommend it for its account of how the Jacquard loom and punch cards led to computers.

z_dt7NG38V4.summary: Eric Bier, a PARC research scientist, demonstrates the Cedar integrated programming environment and language, an evolution of Mesa from Xerox PARC. The demo shows the Tioga editor, garbage collection, and a full graphical workstation environment.
z_dt7NG38V4.why: HN keeps citing it as proof of how advanced a GC-based systems language and integrated workstation were decades ago, and as a model for what desktop OSes could be.

zrpUDuUtxPM.summary: Floyd Toole's CIRMMT distinguished lecture on the science of sound reproduction, drawing on decades of blind listening research. It covers what listeners prefer in loudspeakers and why measured accuracy and anechoic response matter.
zrpUDuUtxPM.why: HN recommends it as a crash course on audio reproduction science, especially the finding that listeners reliably prefer more accurate speakers in blind tests.

zduSFxRajkE.summary: Andrej Karpathy builds the GPT tokenizer from scratch, implementing byte pair encoding along with encode and decode. He shows how many odd LLM behaviors trace back to tokenization, and covers Unicode byte encodings along the way.
zduSFxRajkE.why: Recommended as the best deep dive on tokenizers, worth the two hours for anyone working with LLMs.

zVhQOhxb1Mc.summary: Harvard Belfer Center lecture by Matthew Bunn explaining how nuclear bombs work, including fission and fusion weapons and which parts of bomb-making are hard. It is part 1 of 2 in the Nuclear 101 series.
zVhQOhxb1Mc.why: HN recommends it as an entertaining, clear explanation of nuclear weapons basics from a policy expert.

zcqZHYo7ONs.summary: MinutePhysics, with 3Blue1Brown, explains Bell's theorem using a Venn diagram paradox and polarizing filters. It shows why no local hidden variable theory can reproduce quantum correlations.
zcqZHYo7ONs.why: Repeatedly recommended as the most accessible explanation of Bell's inequality, reducing it to a simple counting problem.

zAFcV7zuUDA.summary: Terry Moore's three-minute TED talk showing a better way to tie shoes, replacing the common granny knot with a square knot so laces stay tied.
zAFcV7zuUDA.why: Recommended as a tiny, useful life hack many commenters adopted for good.

zUyH3XhpLTo.summary: Veritasium explains what a black hole should look like, using J.P. Luminet's 1979 work and a cardboard 3D model to show how light bends around it. It was made just as the first black hole image was released.
zUyH3XhpLTo.why: Recommended for correctly predicting the features of the real black hole image and clearly explaining the lensing physics behind it.

zi0rHwfiX1Q.summary: John Hughes, co-creator of QuickCheck, talks about property-based testing of hard systems. He shows production examples where it found very low-level bugs, including issues in the CAN bus standard.
zi0rHwfiX1Q.why: Recommended as the best introduction to property-based testing and cited for its examples of bugs found in the CAN standard.

zyVTxGpEO30.summary: Raph Koster's 2014 GDC Next talk on what science says about creativity, with practical steps game designers and developers can use to be more creative. It frames creativity as applying existing patterns in new contexts.
zyVTxGpEO30.why: Recommended even to people outside game development as a useful, practical perspective on how creativity works.

z_hm5oX7ZlE.summary: Robert Erdmann, a materials scientist at the Rijksmuseum, gives a PyCon keynote on the ultra-high-resolution imaging of Rembrandt's Night Watch. He covers the automated gantry camera system, the Python software that drives it, and the large volumes of image data involved.
z_hm5oX7ZlE.why: HN commenters recommend it as a technically jaw-dropping talk, and it is the standard reference whenever the Night Watch gigapixel images come up.

zkTf0LmDqKI.summary: A two-minute clip from a 1994 interview with Steve Jobs by the Santa Clara Valley Historical Association. Jobs talks about failure and about how most people never ask for help, recalling that he simply called people to ask.
zkTf0LmDqKI.why: HN commenters return to it as a motivational reminder to not fear failure and to just ask for what you want.

zt0OQb1DBko.summary: Aditya Siram introduces ATS, a statically typed ML-like language that compiles to C and offers type-safe pointer arithmetic and a full proof language. The Strange Loop talk shows off C interop, concurrency and verification features with non-trivial examples.
zt0OQb1DBko.why: Cited in Rust and systems-language threads as the best introduction to ATS, a language claimed to go beyond Rust's safety guarantees.

zxRgfBXn6Mg.summary: An animated account of Day 1 of the Desert Storm air war on 17 January 1991, covering the 2,775 sorties flown against Iraqi strategic targets in the first 24 hours.
zxRgfBXn6Mg.why: Recommended as a deeply researched, visual series that shows how overwhelming the coalition air campaign was.

z8MVKianh54.summary: Aaron Hsu's FnConf18 talk asks whether APL needs a static type system. He argues that APL's expressiveness and rapid iteration already deliver the benefits usually credited to types.
z8MVKianh54.why: HN points to it as the main argument from the array-language camp that types are unnecessary there, and as a nuanced take on typed versus untyped programming.

zSIDRHUWlVo.summary: Dr. Mark Cucuzzella of the Natural Running Center gives a short instructional video on natural running form. It describes the principles of good technique, including barefoot-style mechanics.
zSIDRHUWlVo.why: HN commenters call it the best video on natural running form and link it in running technique threads.

zZ_nI9E9g0I.summary: The first episode of a screencast series building djb's redo build system from scratch in Haskell. It explains the purpose of redo, writes initial code and sets up a GitHub repository.
zZ_nI9E9g0I.why: Recommended to Haskell learners as a rare example of building a real program step by step beyond toy examples.

zeLToGnjIUM.summary: Zig creator Andrew Kelley's RedisConf 2020 talk on modeling data flow with asynchronous I/O in Zig. It explains how Zig's async/await avoids function coloring, and Loris Cro demonstrates OkRedis, a zero-allocation Redis client.
zeLToGnjIUM.why: HN recommends it as the clearest explanation of how Zig achieves colorless async/await.

zmCTmgavkrQ.summary: Isaac Arthur examines the Dark Forest theory, Cixin Liu's proposed solution to the Fermi Paradox in which civilizations stay silent and may destroy any that reveal themselves. He tests the theory's underlying assumptions and arguments.
zmCTmgavkrQ.why: HN commenters point to it as a well-argued rebuttal of Dark Forest axioms, and recommend his wider Fermi Paradox series.

ztspvPYybIY.summary: Ryan Dahl's first presentation of Node.js at JSConf 2009. He pitches event-driven, non-blocking I/O as the motivation, rather than JavaScript itself.
ztspvPYybIY.why: HN recommends it as a classic dev tool pitch with palpable energy, and cites it for why Node was created.

zz4YVJ4aRfg.summary: Rhonda Patrick of FoundMyFitness makes a case for isothiocyanates such as sulforaphane from cruciferous vegetables and broccoli sprouts. It covers cancer, aging, heart disease, brain and behavior, and neurodegeneration, with chapter timestamps.
zz4YVJ4aRfg.why: HN recommends it as a science-backed overview of sulforaphane's health effects, particularly for cancer.

zFhYJRqz_xk.summary: A Kurzgesagt animation about how the immune system constantly detects and kills cells that are turning cancerous. It explains what cancer cells are and why stopping them is so hard.
zFhYJRqz_xk.why: HN recommends it as a clear, accessible introduction to cancer and the immune system.

zQGOcOUBi6s.summary: A Kurzgesagt animation of how the immune system responds to a bacterial infection, depicting immune cells as an army defending the body.
zQGOcOUBi6s.why: HN suggests it as a simple, layman-friendly explanation of the immune system, especially during COVID vaccine discussions.

zU7Lww-sBPg.summary: Synthetic organic chemist James Tour gives a lecture arguing that origin-of-life research is far from explaining how life began. The talk was published by the Discovery Institute and drew sharp criticism.
zU7Lww-sBPg.why: Recommended by some as a blunt expert critique of origin-of-life research, while others question its claims and length.

za56H2BGamQ.summary: CityNerd Ray Delahanty explains induced demand and what happens when freeways are widened. He walks through the economics of supply and demand applied to traffic and asks how much new traffic appears and whether congestion returns.
za56H2BGamQ.why: HN commenters link it as a clearer explanation of induced demand for people who have not studied the topic.

zDEpeWQHtFU.summary: Glenn Vanderburg argues at the O'Reilly Software Architecture Conference that software development is an engineering discipline, even if immature. He contends the discredited body of knowledge called software engineering has led people to wrongly reject the label.
zDEpeWQHtFU.why: Recommended in debates over whether software is real engineering, as a well-argued case that building is cheap relative to simulating.

zaXKQ70q4KQ.summary: Veritasium tells the story of Kary Mullis, the surfer and LSD user who invented PCR and won a Nobel Prize. It explains how PCR works and how it was developed at Cetus.
zaXKQ70q4KQ.why: Recommended as one of the most accessible introductions to PCR and its history.

zyQwAhppWj8.summary: A roughly 3.5-hour Gamers Nexus investigation into rising PC component prices, driven largely by AI data-center demand for memory and other hardware. It draws on interviews with industry figures to argue that personal computing and ownership are being eroded.
zyQwAhppWj8.why: Recommended as a documentary on the hardware shortage told from the perspective of consumer-facing companies, and cited in threads on RAM prices and ownership.

z71h9XZbAWY.summary: A short tour of the Megaprocessor, a microprocessor built at enormous scale from tens of thousands of discrete transistors. The builder shows what the machine is made of and where it now lives, at the Centre for Computing History in Cambridge, where visitors can play Tetris on it.
z71h9XZbAWY.why: HN commenters link it as the easy way to see the giant home-built CPU without hammering the author's website.

z7ihNLEDiuM.summary: A short clip of Neil deGrasse Tyson answering a question about why there are not more women in science. He describes the resistance he faced as a Black kid pursuing science and the systemic barriers many people encounter.
z7ihNLEDiuM.why: Linked in diversity-in-tech threads as a personal, thoughtful answer on systemic barriers for minorities and women in science.

zBgCRJluWTc.summary: Dr. K of HealthyGamerGG explains why people feel unmotivated and unable to start tasks after hours of YouTube or similar distractions. He frames it as a result of how social media is designed to capture attention, and says not to blame yourself.
zBgCRJluWTc.why: Recommended in Ask HN threads on motivation and internet addiction as an accessible explanation of why screen time dulls drive.

zT58pzY41wA.summary: AVweb's Paul Bertorelli analyzes the safety record of the Cirrus Airframe Parachute System (CAPS), looking at the 90-plus deployments over 20 years of Cirrus flying. He asks whether the whole-aircraft parachute has actually saved lives.
zT58pzY41wA.why: Cited in aviation-accident threads as a compact analysis of whether whole-aircraft parachutes work, with the track record described as impressive.

zaUCDZ9d09Y.summary: Thunderf00t critiques Starlink's economics and technical claims alongside other unfulfilled Musk promises. It argues Starlink is a poor business.
zaUCDZ9d09Y.why: Mostly cited as a contrarian critique of Starlink's viability; some defend its economics argument while others dismiss it as repetitive.

zdkyGDqU7xA.summary: Tech Ingredients shows how to build cheap, high-performance flat-panel speakers using audio exciters on sheet materials such as foam-core board. It explains how distributed-mode speakers work and walks through experiments to find good designs.
zdkyGDqU7xA.why: Pointed to by hobbyists interested in building flat-panel DIY speakers from cheap materials.

zmeDzx4SUME.summary: A short clip from Udacity's Web Development course in which Reddit co-founder Steve Huffman describes how Reddit grew early on. He explains seeding the site with content from fake accounts.
zmeDzx4SUME.why: HN cites it as a first-hand admission from a founder of how Reddit seeded content with fake users, in threads on bootstrapping user-generated sites.

zsjZ2r9Ygzw.summary: John Oliver's Last Week Tonight segment on encryption and the Apple versus FBI dispute after San Bernardino. It explains the stakes of weakening encryption and ends with a fake Apple ad about iPhone vulnerabilities.
zsjZ2r9Ygzw.why: Cited in encryption policy threads as a funny, accessible primer and for its fake Apple ad.

ztAg643gJBA.summary: Jeija demonstrates a modified Minetest game with a spherical planet, using a grid transform to make a voxel world round. It includes the orbit math and download links for the spheretest build.
ztAg643gJBA.why: Pointed to in Minetest and spherical-voxel-world threads as a striking example of what the open-source engine can do.

zuKV2DI9-Jg.summary: A School of Life video arguing that everyone marries someone who is somewhat wrong for them, and that this is unavoidable. It is a four-minute version of an essay by Alain de Botton.
zuKV2DI9-Jg.why: HN points to it as the short cliff's-notes version of the essay and as a charming introduction to The School of Life.

z9quxZsLcfo.summary: A Thoughtworks conversation among Martin Fowler, Kent Beck and David Heinemeier Hansson on whether TDD is dead. They discuss the tradeoffs of test-driven development, mocking and where TDD helps or hurts design.
z9quxZsLcfo.why: Recommended in TDD and unit-testing threads as a balanced debate among three prominent developers that avoids dogma.

zQTfuI-9jIo.summary: Stuart Armstrong of the Future of Humanity Institute gives an Oxford physics talk on what exploratory engineering suggests about the Fermi paradox. He argues that von Neumann probes and Dyson spheres are plausibly buildable and asks what traces advanced civilizations would leave.
zQTfuI-9jIo.why: Cited as a source for the feasibility of colonizing the universe with self-replicating probes and for building a Dyson swarm from Mercury.

zprSxCMlECA.summary: Freespin is a demo that runs on a Commodore 1541 floppy drive. It makes sound by vibrating the drive head and video by toggling the serial bus lines, and it keeps running after the C64 that booted it is disconnected.
zprSxCMlECA.why: Shared as a favorite example of retrocomputing hackery, a demo that runs entirely on a disk drive.

z-q8ehzHeQQ.summary: A Technology Connections video on JVC's LCCS, a display hybrid that cycles a color LCD shutter over a monochrome CRT to produce field-sequential color without dots or stripes. It builds on his earlier videos about analog TV and compatible color.
z-q8ehzHeQQ.why: HN links it as a neat breakdown of an unusual CRT/LCD color technology.

z2_dhUv_CrI.summary: A clip from The Simpsons episode 'Krusty Gets Kancelled' showing 'Worker and Parasite', an Eastern European take on Itchy and Scratchy. It is reportedly one of Matt Groening's favorite moments from the show.
z2_dhUv_CrI.why: HN brings it up as a funny parody of odd Eastern European cartoons and as a joke about automation or replaced entertainment.

z8VhNF_0I5c.summary: A 47-minute restoration of a 1920s IBM computing cheese cutter, a machine with parts patented between 1901 and 1907. The video covers the restoration work and explains why it is a computing cheese cutter.
z8VhNF_0I5c.why: HN shares it as a fun curiosity about early IBM history, with time stamps for the nameplate and the explanation.

z9UjeTMb3Yk.summary: Merlin Mann's 2007 Google Tech Talk on Inbox Zero, covering Getting Things Done, why an empty inbox matters, and strategies for handling high-volume email. It is a talk on attention and processing mail rather than on emptying it for its own sake.
z9UjeTMb3Yk.why: Cited as the original Inbox Zero talk, and for Mann's point that optimizing how you organize tasks is no substitute for doing them.

zBnDWSvaQ1I.summary: A creator runs an informal live test of whether Google or Facebook listen through the microphone to target ads, using Chrome on Windows 10. The description admits the methodology is flawed, including that live streaming itself records the microphone.
zBnDWSvaQ1I.why: Cited in threads about phones listening for ads as an anecdotal demonstration, though other commenters doubt it.

zGcKURD_osM.summary: A ColdFusion documentary on the Sackler family and Purdue Pharma, tracing their role in the opioid crisis that has killed over 200,000 people.
zGcKURD_osM.why: Used as background viewing in threads on Purdue's bankruptcy and opioid settlements.

zJOS0sV2a24.summary: Randall Munroe, creator of xkcd, gives an Authors@Google talk in 2007 about the webcomic and his background, followed by audience Q&A. Donald Knuth and Guido van Rossum ask questions during the session.
zJOS0sV2a24.why: HN refers to it for the moment where Knuth asks a question and addresses the Steve Jobs anecdote, a favorite geek moment.

zJdqJu-6ZPo.summary: A speech by comedian Konstantin Kisin at an Oxford Union debate on whether woke culture has gone too far. He argues the case in a short segment of the debate.
zJdqJu-6ZPo.why: HN commenters mostly use it as a side reference in climate-policy threads, pointing to his remarks on sacrifice and failed predictions.

zNT8Zo_sfwo.summary: A clip from the documentary Ride with Larry showing a retired police captain with Parkinson's trying medical marijuana for the first time. The change in tremor, dyskinesia and voice is shown unedited.
zNT8Zo_sfwo.why: Shared as a vivid visual example of cannabis visibly reducing Parkinson's tremor.

zQLUPjefuWA.summary: An excerpt from Hal Abelson's opening SICP lecture introducing computer science and contrasting declarative and imperative knowledge. He argues that computer science is not really a science and is more like magic or engineering of ideas.
zQLUPjefuWA.why: Cited in debates over whether computer science is a science, and for Abelson's line that it is neither a science nor about computers.

zR3Igc3Rhfg.summary: A short film in which friends build the first true-to-scale model of the solar system, with full planetary orbits, on a Nevada dry lakebed. It conveys the real distances and sizes involved.
zR3Igc3Rhfg.why: Shared as the best visceral demonstration of solar system scale.

zRjTyRly5WA.summary: A Gource visualization of 826 days of Minecraft development, from alpha 1.2 to release 1.5, condensed into eight minutes. Each dot is a file, folders are links, and developers fly around zapping files as they work on them.
zRjTyRly5WA.why: Shared as the canonical example of visualizing a real project's version control history with Gource.

zU8alMWUmDI.summary: A tutorial in the GAS Therapy series showing how to recreate the Teenage Engineering OP-1 and OP-1 Field with free software. It argues you do not need to buy expensive gear to make music.
zU8alMWUmDI.why: HN mentions it in threads on the OP-1 and gear acquisition syndrome, as a look at the OP-1's feature set and a cheaper alternative.

z_Ti4GP0ntE.summary: Adam Savage and engineer Kipp Bradford build a compact wearable refrigeration system to keep Adam cool under costumes, modeled on the cooling unit in a NASA spacesuit simulator. It is a long, hands-on build session.
z_Ti4GP0ntE.why: Brought up whenever wearable cooling or heat extremes come up, as a real worked example of a pumped-coolant cooling suit.

zkbPdEHEyEI.summary: Robert Miles covers a paper where researchers ran real versions of his earlier mesa-optimizer thought experiments. They show inner misalignment, where an AI learns the wrong goal in training and misbehaves when deployed.
zkbPdEHEyEI.why: Pointed to as evidence that AI misalignment is an empirically demonstrated problem, for people who dismiss it.

zluKcazgkV4.summary: Roman Elizarov compares Kotlin Coroutines with OpenJDK Project Loom virtual threads, looking at their design goals and how those translate into different implementations and tradeoffs. He addresses how the two can coexist.
zluKcazgkV4.why: Pointed to in Java 21 and Loom discussions as the Kotlin lead's authoritative view on coroutines versus virtual threads.

znQk_yBHre4.summary: The Geopolymer Institute presents Joseph Davidovits's theory that the Egyptian pyramids were built from cast artificial limestone, a geopolymer concrete, rather than carved blocks. It demonstrates how few people could make blocks.
znQk_yBHre4.why: HN brings it up as an alternative, fringe theory about pyramid construction, with one commenter saying it was proved by demonstration and analysis.

zp0OEDcAro0.summary: Chris Houser's Clojure/conj talk on why Clojure's exceptions destroy information as the stack unwinds, unlike Common Lisp's condition system, which can resume from the error site. He surveys the existing libraries that approximate conditions, explains why they don't compose with each other, and considers what a better design would look like.
zp0OEDcAro0.why: Clojure commenters cite it as the best overview of condition systems in Clojure and of the libraries that attempt them.

zqmOSMAtadc.summary: Practical Engineering explains how continuous welded rail copes with thermal expansion by restraining it, using the relationship between temperature, stress and strain. The video is part of a series on railways.
zqmOSMAtadc.why: Linked in rail and heat-related threads as the clear explanation of why railroads need no expansion joints and how heat problems are handled.

ztpcWUqVpIg.summary: Not Just Bikes reflects on five years in the Netherlands and tours small towns and cities, from Haarlem to Veenendaal. It argues that good urbanism with walkable streets, bike infrastructure and transit is found almost everywhere there, not just in Amsterdam.
ztpcWUqVpIg.why: Used as a go-to reference in car-dependence debates to show that small towns and rural areas can work without cars.

z3aEv3EzMyQ.summary: Linus Tech Tips reviews AMD's third-gen Ryzen 9 3900X and Ryzen 7 3700X at launch, testing gaming and workstation performance against Intel.
z3aEv3EzMyQ.why: HN mostly references it for launch benchmarks comparing Ryzen and Intel, rather than recommending it outright.

z4AeoAWGJBw.summary: Musician TheFatRat describes how his video with 47 million views was claimed by another party through YouTube's copyright system and how he got it back.
z4AeoAWGJBw.why: Cited as an example of false copyright claims hitting even popular creators.

z4FGzE4endQ.summary: A Community clip in which Dean Pelton explores a virtual reality environment, including a blooper moment.
z4FGzE4endQ.why: Linked as a joke whenever VR interfaces or headsets are discussed.

z5Otla5157c.summary: The Lonely Island's comedic music video 'YOLO' featuring Adam Levine and Kendrick Lamar.
z5Otla5157c.why: Used as a joke reply in threads about risky decisions, with one commenter calling it hilarious and catchy.

z5e7kWSHWTg.summary: Ryan Florence's React.js Conf 2015 talk pushes React into unusual use cases, including a demo comparing rendering in React, Ember and Angular.
z5e7kWSHWTg.why: Mostly cited for its side-by-side rendering demo in Ember and React performance debates, not as a general recommendation.

z6ep308goxQ.summary: Answer in Progress investigates why Japanese websites look different from those elsewhere, using an AI clustering approach to test the 2013 claim. It then looks at possible explanations.
z6ep308goxQ.why: Cited as a companion to articles on Japanese web design and as an example of clustering websites by appearance.

z7sHc4P4zPg.summary: A three-minute culture video from Nylas, the email company, showing life at the company as a recruiting piece.
z7sHc4P4zPg.why: Linked repeatedly from Nylas's monthly Who is Hiring job posts as a look at the company culture.

zGK-EzEa45U.summary: A short video of Venetian Snares' track 'Vache' with the Renoise tracker sequencer data scrolling past, uploaded by the artist in 2006 as a demo of the software.
zGK-EzEa45U.why: Cited in tracker and black-MIDI threads as an example of dense breakcore made in Renoise.

zHU1xH6Ogs4.summary: Thomas Garrity discusses mathematical maturity, a concept mathematicians use for professional development, and how it can inform teaching, mentoring and careers. It was given at the IAS/PCMI Park City Mathematics Institute.
zHU1xH6Ogs4.why: HN mostly cites it as a source or related clip in math and neural network discussions, not as a strong recommendation.

zIE-5hg7FoA.summary: A home VCR recording of the original Apple '1984' Macintosh ad, directed by Ridley Scott, as it aired during Super Bowl XVIII, shown in the context of the broadcast.
zIE-5hg7FoA.why: Mostly invoked ironically, to contrast Apple's anti-Big-Brother image in 1984 with its present-day behavior.

zILwgQhjC_Q.summary: Dave Jones of EEVblog demonstrates that a frequency counter can detect gravity through the 2g tipover effect on quartz crystal oscillators. He shows the reading shift as the instrument's orientation changes.
zILwgQhjC_Q.why: HN links it as a hands-on demonstration that oscillator frequency depends on orientation relative to gravity.

zKgN2G9d0dc.summary: A two-minute Telegraph report that takes a decibel meter to a wind farm and nearby residential areas to measure how loud turbines are compared with everyday noise.
zKgN2G9d0dc.why: HN cites it in wind-power debates as measured evidence that turbine noise is low relative to ambient or road noise.

zN_Zl64OQEw.summary: Cockpit camera footage of a jet hitting a bird after takeoff, losing its engine and the crew ejecting. Commenters note it is actually a Canadian CT-155 Hawk despite the F16 title.
zN_Zl64OQEw.why: Cited as a vivid example of bird strikes and ejection, in threads on drones, aircraft collisions and ejections.

zP0sqRMzkwo.summary: A Monty Python's Flying Circus sketch in which a job interview descends into absurdity, with Portuguese subtitles. It is a short comedy bit about nonsensical interviews.
zP0sqRMzkwo.why: HN references it as a joke about silly or absurd hiring practices.

zYTxuW2vmzk.summary: Al Jazeera's full unedited version of the WikiLeaks 'Collateral Murder' footage from a US military helicopter cockpit, showing a 2007 Baghdad attack that killed about a dozen people, including two Reuters journalists.
zYTxuW2vmzk.why: HN cites it as primary evidence of US conduct in Iraq and as the leak most associated with Julian Assange's prosecution.

z_wImaGRkNY.summary: A short Conan on TBS segment mocking Apple's new wireless AirPods and the removal of the iPhone 7 headphone jack, in the form of a parody ad.
z_wImaGRkNY.why: HN mentions it only in passing as a joke about AirPods.

zaRHU1XxMJQ.summary: A short screen capture of SGI's File System Navigator (FSN, also called Fusion) running on IRIX 6.5 on an Octane. It shows the 3D file browser seen in Jurassic Park.
zaRHU1XxMJQ.why: Linked as proof that the 3D file manager in Jurassic Park was a real Unix application, in threads on movie UIs.

zaT7thTxyq8.summary: An Opera browser promotional video from 2010 in which a browser races a potato in a tongue-in-cheek speed test.
zaT7thTxyq8.why: Mostly brought up ironically, as a remembered ad or joke when browser speed claims come up.

zcoYKuoiUrY.summary: A long video essay examining the 2017 Unite the Right rally in Charlottesville, with footage and commentary on the neo-Nazi participants. It draws on rally footage, VICE News, and the Hunton & Williams report.
zcoYKuoiUrY.why: Referenced as evidence of the Nazi iconography and chants at the rally, in arguments over how to characterize it.

zdHkY3XYHKA.summary: An animated map of the territories of Chinese dynasties from 1000 BC to the present, compressed into about a minute.
zdHkY3XYHKA.why: Cited in passing to show how China's borders have expanded and contracted over history.

zdKCQKBvH-A.summary: JJRicks rides a driverless Waymo in Phoenix when it gets confused by traffic cones, blocks traffic, and evades the support vehicles sent to retrieve it. The episode is one of a long series of rider-view Waymo videos.
zdKCQKBvH-A.why: Cited in self-driving threads as a documented case of a robotaxi failing at traffic cones, with some comments also noting the support team response.

zfR_Jj4grZE.summary: A 2017 Apple TV commercial for the iPad Pro in which a kid asks "What's a computer?" while using the tablet. It pitches the all-screen iPad Pro as something that goes beyond what people think of as a computer.
zfR_Jj4grZE.why: Cited as a concise example of Apple and the wider tech industry framing devices as anything but a personal computer.

zhPklt9nYas.summary: Google's "Dear Sophie" Chrome ad, in which a father emails his daughter's life moments to her future self over the years. It portrays an email account as a lifelong keepsake.
zhPklt9nYas.why: Brought up ironically in threads about Google deleting inactive accounts and tightening storage policies, as a reminder that Google once encouraged this kind of long-term use.

zhr6fHmCJ6k.summary: A one-minute montage of Elon Musk promising Tesla robotaxis would arrive "next year" over eight years. It was published by Dan O'Dowd's media channel, which campaigns against Tesla's self-driving software.
zhr6fHmCJ6k.why: Used as a compact exhibit of Musk's repeatedly missed self-driving timelines, not as a recommendation.

zicGxU5MfwE.summary: NBC New York clip of President Trump at an April 2020 press conference asking whether disinfectant could be injected as a coronavirus treatment, following a presentation on sunlight and decontamination.
zicGxU5MfwE.why: Used mainly as a political reference in arguments over what Trump actually said and in criticism of him, not as something to learn from.

zihTWh5i2C4.summary: Ray Kurzweil presents his book How to Create a Mind at Google, on reverse engineering the brain and using that understanding to build intelligent machines. He shows his graphs of exponential technological progress.
zihTWh5i2C4.why: Linked in threads about Kurzweil joining Google, mostly as a source for his exponential progress charts and his ambitions there.

ziqpwkhqTRs.summary: Archive footage from 1964 of Royal Marine Commando volunteers filmed on a field exercise after taking LSD at Porton Down. It documents a British military drug trial.
ziqpwkhqTRs.why: HN cites it as evidence for strange military experiments, in particular soldiers being dosed with LSD to test their performance.

zjJ2-cdhwMQ.summary: Charbax interviews the CEO and CMO of CLEARink at SID Display Week 2019 about their eTIR reflective display technology. It demos 9.7-inch low-power color and video ePaper with high refresh capability.
zjJ2-cdhwMQ.why: Cited by e-ink enthusiasts as the main look at CLEARink, a hoped-for next-generation reflective display startup.

zn2Xf9hAFcE.summary: A scene from the 2011 film Margin Call in which risk head Eric Dale is laid off by HR and hands a USB stick to a young analyst. It shows a scripted, impersonal corporate firing.
zn2Xf9hAFcE.why: Referenced as the canonical depiction of mass layoffs and canned HR scripts whenever layoffs come up.

zn7-fVtT16k.summary: An Epic Rap Battles of History episode in which Albert Einstein and Stephen Hawking trade rap verses. It is a popular comedic music video.
zn7-fVtT16k.why: Shared as a joke in threads about Einstein, physics and famous scientists.

zqEvQKO5_gM.summary: A short Newsweek clip of White House press secretary Jen Psaki saying the administration is flagging problematic posts to Facebook that spread COVID-19 and vaccine disinformation.
zqEvQKO5_gM.why: Cited as the admission that the government flagged posts to platforms, in debates over government involvement in content moderation.

zqyZ9bFl_qg.summary: A short animation illustrating the proposed nanofactory concept, where nanomachines assemble atomically precise parts into larger products. It depicts how such a system might build macroscopic goods from raw materials and energy.
zqyZ9bFl_qg.why: Shared as a visualization of Ralph Merkle's theoretical work on molecular manufacturing.

zrv78nG9R04.summary: A Radio Free Asia report from its China food safety series on how "gutter oil" is recovered from sewers and waste and sold on to cheap restaurants and street vendors.
zrv78nG9R04.why: Cited as a documentary look at gutter oil and as an example of restaurant cost-cutting and food safety problems.

zrzMhU_4m-g.summary: The 'She's a witch!' scene from Monty Python and the Holy Grail, in which villagers reason absurdly about how to identify a witch.
zrzMhU_4m-g.why: Posted almost purely as a joke reference when a thread's logic resembles the scene.

ztsi0CLxmjw.summary: Henry Segerman and collaborators demonstrate virtual reality experiences in non-Euclidean spaces, including hyperbolic and mixed hyperbolic-Euclidean geometry. The browser-based demos let viewers move through these spaces and show how strange the geometry feels from inside.
ztsi0CLxmjw.why: Cited as the go-to example of hyperbolic geometry made intuitive through VR.

zyaocKS3sfg.summary: Adam Savage builds a Victorian-style rickshaw carriage for Boston Dynamics' Spot robot to pull, with him riding as passenger. The video covers the build and the engineering problems of pairing cutting-edge robotics with vintage transport, such as tuning the payload through Spot's API.
zyaocKS3sfg.why: HN commenters cite it as a fun real-world example of Spot hauling a passenger whenever Boston Dynamics robots come up.
